title: Watchlist Architecture Addendum v3 — payout-edit route ownership, NEW email-test route, D43 sort enforcement, attribute-column inventory + credit-day CHECK migration, candidate-whitelist supersede, #returns link contract (D42/D43)

sections.heading: Payout-edit route ownership — existing payment POST + payment_ledger as the single truth (D42)
sections.body: DELTA over Watchlist_Architecture_Addendum_v2: the D42 editable payout cell creates NO new writer and NO new table. The Payouts cell editor maps onto the EXISTING POST /payment/<bond_id>/<month> route (payment_edit in src/app.py, GET+POST), which owns the payment_ledger row for (bond_id, month): amount and paid flag. Cell semantics per the locked design v6: an empty amount saves as Missed (Danger chip), amount with received renders 'amount + checkmark', amount without received renders 'amount + pending'; Save posts through the route, then the row's payment health re-derives at read time from payment_ledger — the v2 data_ownership rule stands: nothing stores health, two reads over unchanged data agree. payment_ledger remains the ONLY truth for Received, for the dashboard tiles, for exports/print and for the D42 returns aggregation; because the editor is a thin UI over the existing route, every downstream surface sees the edit with no sync job and no second endpoint (F-233 seam: payment editor maps to existing POST payment route + payment_ledger). Month columns on this surface are elapsed + current only, newest-left (D42; the F-231 future-column lesson), and row order comes from the shared D43 sort key defined in the sort-enforcement section — never from template logic. FR ids cited here (FR-67, FR-68) are provisional pending PRD v6 (brief 36a, parallel).

sections.heading: NEW email-test route — alert_prefs key/value persistence + mailer.py send path (D42)
sections.body: The D42 Send test email action needs a NEW route (POST /settings/email/test) because the shipped app has no test-send endpoint (F-233 seam: email test = NEW route persisting via alert_prefs). Ownership split: (1) THE ROUTE reads the Settings form and the provider presets — Gmail = smtp.gmail.com / 587 / TLS, Outlook / Microsoft 365 = smtp.office365.com / 587 / STARTTLS, Custom = cleared fields (D42 email presets, App-Password-only research: less-secure-apps is dead) — and validates before sending; (2) PERSISTENCE uses the EXISTING alert_prefs key/value table (src/db.py; the INSERT OR REPLACE pattern already exercised by src/app.py and src/notifications.py) with namespaced keys for non-secret config and last-test status only — the SMTP App Password is NEVER written to alert_prefs values that render, never returned in a banner and never logged; credentials stay in the environment variables src/mailer.py already reads (SMTP_HOST / SMTP_PORT / SMTP_USER / SMTP_APP_PASSWORD); (3) THE SEND runs through src/mailer.py (the shared smtplib path behind send_alert_email: STARTTLS on 587 or SMTP_SSL on 465, named errors ERR-smtp-unconfigured and ERR-email-send preserved); (4) THE RESPONSE drives the design-v6 banner states — success class with 'Test email sent. Check the inbox (and the spam folder).' versus failure class with 'Sending failed. Authentication failed = usually needs an App Password. Also check SMTP host, port and security setting.'. No new table, no schema change: alert_prefs key/value IS the persistence layer for this route. FR-72 id provisional pending PRD v6 (brief 36a, parallel).

sections.heading: D43 sort enforcement points — ONE shared sort key at query or model layer, never per-template (D43 LOCKED)
sections.body: D43 is LOCKED: Danger -> On-going -> Completed/Matured on EVERY list surface, with the status taxonomy (Danger = immediate attention required; On-going = active and progressing normally; Completed/Matured = successfully finished) and the automatic Danger rule (credit day passed with no payment entered by the due date -> Danger the same day). Enforcement architecture: exactly ONE shared ordering function fed by the engine sort key HEALTH_ORDER = {Danger: 0, On-going: 1, Matured: 2, Invalid: 3} (src/engine.py — sort_payout_rows and the health-order key; Invalid sorts last per the design legend), applied ONCE per request at the QUERY or MODEL layer alongside the parameterized read and the fixed sort whitelist that v1/v2 already mandate. NEVER per-template sorting: templates receive pre-sorted rows and contain no order logic; no screen, export or print path may reimplement the order. Surface inventory (the D43 table every doc must carry): dashboard chart rows and stat-derived lists, My Holdings registry, Payouts grid rows, CSV export (/export.csv), print statement (/print) and the alerts feed — each consumes the shared key; the automatic Danger rule feeds it through read-time derive (arch-v2 data_ownership), and display-label mapping (Returned -> Received, Completed -> Matured) stays render-only so engine values order while labels only display. This section supersedes any per-screen ordering language in arch-v2, which predates the D43 lock. FR-70/FR-71 ids provisional pending PRD v6 (brief 36a, parallel).

sections.heading: Attribute-column inventory — FR-40 set + broker, bonds ALTER list, credit-day CHECK migration 1..28 -> 1..31 (D42 / F-233)
sections.body: Inventory for the D42 attribute-parity feature: (1) ALREADY ON bonds — the FR-40 display set (company, ISIN, rating, coupon, est. yield, invested amount, start/end dates, credit_day, source note) plus broker, which D41 added as a bonds column; these need no new DDL, only form and strip wiring. (2) REQUIRE bonds ALTER (new columns, nullable TEXT/numeric, added in one migration pass): rating_agency, issuer_type, secured, face_value, payout_cycle — the five fields the locked design v6 collects on Add Candidate and shows in both the Watchlist Details facts grid and the My Holdings attribute strip. (3) SCHEMA GATE (F-233 seam): the shipped credit_day CHECK in src/db.py reads CHECK (credit_day >= 1 AND credit_day <= 28) and MUST be migrated to 1..31 (D41 owner rule, carried into the D42 round) via table rebuild that preserves every row — without the migration any insert of credit_day=31 fails even though the forms expose 1..31. Migration ordering: the CHECK rebuild runs first (development-order step 1), the attribute ALTERs second (step 4) — one migration train on the same bonds table, two ordered passes, never two conflicting rebuilds. (4) SURFACES: attributes are collected at candidate entry, optionally completed in the inline move panel (credit day, broker), and displayed identically in the Details facts grid and the holdings strip (parity is a test gate, not a convention); the read path stays one parameterized query with the fixed column whitelist — the whitelist grows to the D42 set, nothing else changes. FR-69/FR-74 ids provisional pending PRD v6 (brief 36a, parallel).

sections.heading: Supersede note — arch-v2 candidate whitelist extended to the D42 attribute set (D42)
sections.body: The v2 view_layer_restructure section fixed the Watchlist candidates-only whitelist at the FR-56 column set (Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Est. Yield, Source note, Action — plus Broker after D41) and pinned the Add Candidate entry form to the same research fields. That text PREDATES D42 (F-233: arch-v2 candidate whitelist text predates D42) and is hereby SUPERSEDED on exactly one point: the candidate entry form and Details facts grid now carry the full D42 attribute set — rating agency, issuer type, secured, face value, payout cycle, invested amount, broker, source note — collected at candidate entry and displayed in the expanded Details facts grid, with the row's visible columns staying the compact design-v6 whitelist (Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Est. Yield, Broker, Status, Details, Action). Everything else in the v2 whitelist text STANDS UNCHANGED: /watch remains candidates-only, watch_state='watching' rows only, no Invested/Received/Next Payout columns and no payment-health chips exist anywhere on that screen, and the ownership boundary (a candidate owns no ledger rows) is untouched. No other v2 section is affected by this supersede; the extension implements the D42 attribute-parity decision at the watchlist half of the parity pair.

sections.heading: #returns link navigation contract — view switch + dashboard tab activation (D42 / F-233)
sections.body: Contract for the Financial Goals KPI links ('Earned this month' and 'Total received' cards each render 'View full returns history on Dashboard' targeting #returns): clicking the link MUST perform THREE steps in one handler, with no server round trip — (1) VIEW SWITCH: the active sidebar view becomes Dashboard (Dashboard marked active, Financial Goals and every other view hidden); (2) TAB ACTIVATION: inside the Dashboard the Returns history tab becomes active and the Overview panel hides (the Overview/Returns history tab pair from design v6); (3) ANCHOR: the page lands on the returns card carrying id 'returns'. A cold load of /goals#returns (or any deep link carrying #returns) must run the same switch + activation on first paint — F-233 seam: the Goals #returns link needs view+tab JS, it does not happen by itself. The link NEVER navigates to a separate route: returns history stays a Dashboard TAB under D42 (Q9 placement), not its own page, so /goals and / remain the only view routes. The tab's data contract (aggregation owned by development-order step 7): payment_ledger GROUP BY month, interest received per month, positions paid-dot-pending of the active set, cumulative running total, newest-first with the current month highlighted — consumed by the same shared-read rules every surface uses. FR-73 id provisional pending PRD v6 (brief 36a, parallel).
